newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels arrested after Bogota police station blast.
newsitem.headline: Rebels arrested after Bogota police station blast.

text.p: Five leftist guerrillas were arrested on Wednesday in raids carried out after an explosion that killed eight policemen and injured more than 10 others, authorities said.

The National Police identified the suspects, three men and two women, as known members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC). The statement made no direct link between the rebels and the blast late on Tuesday in the parking lot of a police station in the Fontibon district in southwest Bogota.

But it said one of the rebels detained, identified by the alias "El Venao" (The Deer), was the head of an urban rebel commando group that attacked a police station last year in Ciudad Kennedy, a working-class district in southern Bogota.

"They're terrorists," National Police chief Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said of the suspects, using the term the army employs in referring to the FARC. "They want to destabilise and frighten," he told reporters.
In raids on two rebel safehouses in the capital early on Wednesday, police said they seized an arsenal that included 40 machetes and 64 rocket-propelled grenades and mortar rounds.

It was not immediately clear if any of the suspects would be charged with planting the bomb that exploded in the back of a truck that had been pulled into the police station parking lot on suspicion of carrying contraband goods. The explosion killed six officers and two patrolmen.
The truck's driver has also been arrested in connection with the blast, which police sources say may have been detonated by remote control.
Serrano offered a $100,000 reward for information leading to more arrests in the case on Wednesday.
The FARC, Colombia's oldest and largest guerrilla army, was founded as a pro-Cuban Marxist group in 1964.
